rv.q: Forty years after its Broadway debut titillated and outraged American theatergoers, this Harold Pinter masterpiece of family warfare continues to unsettle.
Daniel Sullivan's astute direction captures the distinct rhythms of Pinter's dialogue, as the production casts a strange spell that grips you tight.
As a result the shocking ending falls flat and the play’s reputation outshines Mr. Sullivan’s tame production.

tn.cat: Best Featured Actor in a Play

cn.t: Pinter's classic proves "as big as its reputation" in this first-rate revival, with critics praising its pitch-black humor and provocative power, though one finds the acclaimed work doesn't live up to its legendary status.

vs.sum: A beautifully restored theater with a stunning Tiffany-inspired interior. The 2021 renovation transformed restroom facilities from among Broadway's worst to a model for the industry, with modern bathrooms on every public level.

acc.note: Elevator to Mezzanine, Balcony, and lower level restrooms. 7 wheelchair spaces across all levels.
